How the scores work

Scores use National Weather Service hourly data. The best pair of consecutive hours scores as well as its weaker hour, with a deduction for changing wind in the Hunting Forecast. Only full remaining hours count today. Times are Central.

Each hour starts at 100. Subtract 1.5 per degree outside the preferred range (up to 38), 1.8 per mph above the steady wind threshold, and 2 per mph above the gust threshold. When gust data is missing, steady wind stands in. Each activity also deducts a share of the precipitation chance. When precipitation is in the forecast, the rain deduction uses at least 55%.

  • Fishing Forecast. Daylight near the water. Mild temperatures, lower rain chances, and light winds score highest. Gusts of 24 mph or higher rule out a window. Preferred temperature 50–82°F. Wind and gust deductions begin above 8 and 14 mph. Rain weight 0.7.
  • Hunting Forecast. Daylight conditions for the outing. Wind direction changes between hours reduce the score. Gusts of 32 mph or higher rule out a window. Preferred temperature 32–65°F. Wind and gust deductions begin above 10 and 18 mph. Rain weight 0.58.
  • Walking & Running. 6 AM–9 PM Central. Uses feels-like temperature when available, rain chance, and wind. Gusts of 30 mph or higher rule out a window. Preferred temperature 48–72°F. Wind and gust deductions begin above 11 and 18 mph. Rain weight 0.68.
  • Mow-Cast. Daylight only. Rain chance, humidity, and rain in the preceding three hours affect drying potential. Recent station rainfall adds a penalty when available. Gusts of 32 mph or higher rule out a window. Preferred temperature 48–84°F. Wind and gust deductions begin above 12 and 20 mph. Rain weight 0.9.
  • Grilling Forecast. 4–10 PM Central. Scores cool or hot temperatures, gusts, and rain. Gusts of 25 mph or higher or a relevant NWS fire-weather alert rule out a window. Preferred temperature 50–84°F. Wind and gust deductions begin above 9 and 13 mph. Rain weight 0.78.
  • Outdoor Plans Forecast. 6 AM–9 PM Central. Mild temperatures, lower rain chances, and lighter winds score highest for picnics, ballgames, and other outdoor plans. Gusts of 30 mph or higher rule out a window. Preferred temperature 55–82°F. Wind and gust deductions begin above 12 and 18 mph. Rain weight 0.82.

A window needs a score of 65 or higher and a verified NWS alert check. Thunderstorms, freezing precipitation, dangerous temperatures, and relevant active alerts rule out overlapping windows. Drying potential is a weather estimate.
